title: Stevenston: the estate network
standfirst: Tenants at Ardeer Nether, Brakpleuch and Corsankell belong to one estate landscape. The records show neighbourhood and associates, not a ready-made family tree.
question: Can the Mathie-Glencairn records identify a kinship bridge between the Ayrshire tenants and Glasgow burgesses?
answer: Matthew at Ardeer Nether and Michael at Brakpleuch are distinct men in the 1559–60 teind list. Michael in a 1549 sasine is probably the later tenant. Mathie witnesses and later Glencairn households form a useful social corridor, but no surviving record says that these Glasgows were siblings or burgess relatives.

chapters.title: Separate tenants in one landscape
body: A 1549 Stevenston sasine gives a probable earlier occurrence of Michael; the 1559–60 teind list separately places Matthew at Ardeer Nether and Michael at Brakpleuch.
The distinction is important: shared locality does not collapse Matthew and Michael into one person or one household.

evidence.label: Michael: separate identity and estate records

chapters.title: Corsankell supplies a documented family
body: The nearby Corsankell charter does name James elder's sons, providing a firmly defined household inside the broader estate setting.
It does not say that Matthew or Michael belonged to that household.

chapters.title: Mathie and Glencairn as a research corridor
body: Robert the fisher and David Mathie appear together in 1554; later Mathie and Glencairn records create a route worth testing.
A later Mathie marriage connection is a lead only. It supplies neither a stated tenant relationship nor a burgh-to-Ayrshire descent.
